caveats.title: Before you quote these numbers
caveats.1: These are receipts from crops alone, for six months. They are not household incomes: wages, livestock and other work are left out.
caveats.2: Only paid-out costs are subtracted. Family labour, seed saved from the last harvest and the household's own land cost nothing here, so the real return to farming is lower.
caveats.3: January to June is mostly the rabi season. States that rely on the kharif crop look poorer here than they would over a full year.
caveats.4: Amounts are in 2013 rupees, not adjusted for inflation.
caveats.5: The ranges cover sampling error only, not mistakes in recall or valuation. For small states the range is wide; quote it.
caveats.6: Large farms pull the average up. The median household receives much less than the average, so quote both.

method.title: How these numbers were made
method.p1: The National Statistical Office surveyed {households} agricultural households in {villages} villages between August and December 2013, asking what crops they produced from January to June. The household records come from microdata.gov.in; for each household, the value of its crops and its paid-out expenses were added up.
method.p2: Every figure uses NSSO's survey weights, so it speaks for India's {millions} million ({crore} crore) agricultural households, not only the sample. The 95% ranges allow for how the survey was drawn: villages within districts, then households within villages.
method.p3: Before anything is published, the All-India figures are checked against NSSO's own report, Key Indicators of Situation of Agricultural Households in India (2014):
check.output_per_cultivator: Value of crops per household that grew them (₹)
tool.title: Get these numbers yourself
tool.lead: The same toolkit downloads any survey on microdata.gov.in, and in Google Colab it needs no coding.
tool.step1: Make a free account on microdata.gov.in and create an API key on your profile page.
tool.step2: Open the notebook in Google Colab and save the key in Colab's Secrets panel.
tool.step3: Press Run all. The notebook downloads the files, checks them against NSSO's report and writes the state tables.
